tasks.title: Bootstrap Spring Boot 4 / Java 25 Maven project, profiles config and build gates (pom, it profile, springdoc dump)
definition_of_done: pom.xml declares Java 25 / Spring Boot 4 with spring-boot-starter-web, validation, data-jpa, data-redis, flyway-core, postgresql driver, springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui, and test scope: spring-boot-starter-test, testcontainers (postgresql, junit-jupiter) plus a Redis container dependency

pom.xml defines a `it` Maven profile that binds maven-failsafe-plugin (verify) for **/*IT.java AND runs spring-boot-maven-plugin start/stop around integration-test with springdoc-openapi-maven-plugin writing target/openapi.json (or target/openapi.yaml)
surefire runs only unit tests (**/*Test.java) so `./mvnw -q test` never needs Docker
spotless-maven-plugin configured so `./mvnw -q spotless:check` passes on committed sources
ShortenerProperties exposes base-url (default http://localhost:8080), redis counter batch size (default 1000), default cache TTL (24h per AMB-9) and counter seed offset (AMB-11)
application.yml holds shared config; application-read.yml / application-write.yml document the read/write deployment profiles; no secrets or credentials literals beyond local defaults
ShortenerPropertiesTest asserts the documented defaults without booting a database
`./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile`, `./mvnw -q test` and `./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test` pass with the provisioned mvnw and sdlc/ArchitectureTest.java untouched
tasks.risk_notes: Touches protected pom.xml and application*.yml (dependency + config surface). Spring Boot 4 / Java 25 coordinates and the springdoc maven plugin wiring are the highest-risk items; a wrong `it` profile breaks the contract gate for every later task. ArchitectureTest is orchestrator-provisioned and its package rules are unknown - keep the com.example.shortener package layering conventional.
tasks.rollback_note: Revert pom.xml and src/main/resources/application*.yml plus the two new java files; repo returns to the provisioned-wrapper-only state.

tasks.title: Flyway migration for urls table + counter sequence, JPA entity and repository
data_model_slice: urls.created_by (varchar null, always null in this scenario)
definition_of_done: V1__create_urls_table.sql creates the urls table with short_code primary key, long_url, created_at, expires_at, created_by (nullable), code_source, plus an index supporting expiry lookups and a Postgres sequence url_code_seq seeded past the AMB-11 offset
UrlMapping is a JPA entity mapped 1:1 to the migration columns; CodeSource enum has REDIS('redis') and DB_SEQUENCE('db_sequence')
UrlMappingRepository extends a Spring Data JPA repository with existsByShortCode and findByShortCode, and a native query nextval('url_code_seq')
MigrationScriptTest asserts the migration file exists, is named V1__*, and contains every required column/sequence (no container needed)
UrlMappingTest covers entity expiry helper logic (isExpired at/after expires_at, never expired when null)
`./mvnw -q test` and `./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test` pass
tasks.risk_notes: Touches the protected **/db/migration/** path; the schema is the source of truth for every later task and changing it after integration tests exist means a new versioned migration. created_by must stay nullable and unpopulated (non-goal / PII avoidance).
tasks.rollback_note: Delete the V1 migration and the domain package; no other task has run against the schema yet, so no follow-up migration is needed.

tasks.title: Request/response DTOs, validation rules and problem+json global exception handler
definition_of_done: CreateUrlRequest uses snake_case JSON names (long_url, custom_alias, expiration_date) with Bean Validation: long_url @NotBlank, max 2048, http/https-only pattern; custom_alias optional pattern [0-9a-zA-Z]{3,32}; expiration_date parsed as ISO-8601 OffsetDateTime and required to be in the future

GlobalExceptionHandler is a @RestControllerAdvice extending ResponseEntityExceptionHandler that returns application/problem+json ProblemDetail for 400 (validation + malformed ISO-8601/unreadable body), 404, 409, 410 and unhandled 500 with a consistent body (type/title/status/detail/instance) and no stack traces or internal details leaked
CreateUrlRequestValidationTest covers valid input, ftp scheme, >2048 chars, bad alias charset, alias length 2 and 33, malformed and past expiration_date
GlobalExceptionHandlerTest asserts status, Content-Type application/problem+json and body fields for each mapped exception
`./mvnw -q test`, `./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test` and `./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile` pass
tasks.risk_notes: The error contract shape fixed here is consumed by the OpenAPI document in T7; drift causes a contract gate failure. Problem details must never echo secrets or PII.
tasks.rollback_note: Delete the api/dto and api/error packages plus their tests; nothing else depends on them yet.

tasks.title: Base62 short-code generation: batched Redis INCRBY counter with Postgres-sequence fallback
definition_of_done: RedisBatchCounterSource reserves a range via a single INCRBY <batchSize> (default 1000) on a global key and hands out values from the local range; exhausting the range triggers the next INCRBY; restart gaps are accepted (AMB-10)

ShortCodeAllocator returns AllocatedCode with CodeSource.REDIS normally and falls back to DbSequenceCounterSource (nextval url_code_seq) with CodeSource.DB_SEQUENCE when Redis throws/times out, logging the degradation without leaking connection strings
Counter values are offset by the configured seed so every generated base62 code is at least 3 characters (AMB-11)

Base62CodecTest covers round-trip encoding, alphabet [0-9a-zA-Z], and minimum length after offset; ShortCodeAllocatorTest uses a mocked Redis source to assert fallback path and code_source values; RedisBatchCounterSourceTest asserts exactly one INCRBY per batch and strictly increasing, unique values under concurrent allocation
`./mvnw -q test` and `./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test` pass
tasks.risk_notes: Concurrency correctness (uniqueness across threads/instances) and the Redis-failure detection path are subtle; a too-broad catch could mask real bugs, a too-narrow one breaks AC-11.
tasks.rollback_note: Delete the codegen package and its tests; T5 is the only consumer and has not been built yet.

tasks.title: Write path: POST /api/v1/urls service + profile-gated controller
data_model_slice: urls insert {short_code, long_url, created_at, expires_at, created_by=null, code_source}
definition_of_done: UrlWriteController is annotated @Profile("!read") so it registers under the default and write profiles and is absent under the read profile (AC-14), maps POST /api/v1/urls with operationId createShortUrl, validates the body with @Valid and returns 201 with CreateUrlResponse

UrlWriteService persists a row with created_by left null, uses custom_alias as short_code when supplied, otherwise the allocated base62 code, and records code_source; duplicate alias (pre-check plus DataIntegrityViolation on the PK) raises AliasAlreadyExistsException -> 409 problem+json
Re-posting an existing long_url without an alias always allocates a new distinct code (no deduplication, AC-4)
short_url is composed from the configured base URL (default http://localhost:8080) plus the short code

UrlWriteServiceTest (mocked repository/allocator) covers success, alias conflict, no-dedup, and db_sequence fallback persistence; UrlWriteControllerTest is a @WebMvcTest with the global exception handler asserting 201 payload and 400/409 problem+json responses and that no row is persisted on validation failure
`./mvnw -q test`, `./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test` pass
tasks.risk_notes: Profile predicate must be exactly the agreed semantics ('read' instance -> 404 on POST); a wrong annotation silently breaks AC-14 and the contract gate (endpoint present/absent mismatch).
tasks.rollback_note: Delete the write package and its tests; read path and schema are unaffected.

tasks.title: Read path: Redis-cached redirect service + profile-gated GET /{short_code} controller
data_model_slice: redis key: shortener:url:{short_code} -> long_url (TTL = min(remaining time to expires_at, default 24h))
definition_of_done: RedirectController is annotated @Profile("!write") (registers under default and read profiles, absent under write), maps GET /{short_code} with operationId redirectToLongUrl and returns 302 with Location = long_url and header Cache-Control: private

UrlReadService checks the cache first and skips the Postgres query on a hit; on a miss it loads from the repository and populates the cache with TTL = remaining time to expires_at, capped by the configured default 24h TTL when expires_at is null (AMB-9)
Unknown code -> ShortCodeNotFoundException (404 problem+json); expired code -> ShortCodeExpiredException (410 problem+json) and the cache entry is not served after expiry
Redis failures on get/put are caught, logged as a cache degradation warning (no credentials in the log) and the redirect is served directly from Postgres (AC-13)

UrlReadServiceTest (mocked cache/repository) proves the repository is never touched on a cache hit, covers miss, expired, not-found and Redis-down bypass; RedisUrlCacheTest asserts TTL computation bounds; RedirectControllerTest is a @WebMvcTest asserting 302 + Location + Cache-Control: private and the 404/410 problem+json bodies
`./mvnw -q test`, `./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test` pass
tasks.risk_notes: Cache-hit path must genuinely avoid the datasource (verified by mock interaction) and TTL must never exceed remaining expiry, otherwise stale redirects outlive the link. Profile predicate mistakes break AC-14.
tasks.rollback_note: Delete the read package and its tests; write path and schema unaffected.

tasks.title: Committed OpenAPI document + Testcontainers integration tests (Postgres, Redis, profiles, contract parity)
definition_of_done: src/main/resources/openapi.yaml documents exactly the implemented API: createShortUrl (POST /api/v1/urls: 201, 400, 409, all error responses application/problem+json) and redirectToLongUrl (GET /{short_code}: 302 with Location and Cache-Control headers, 404, 410) with schemas matching the DTO JSON names, and no extra or missing operations/status codes
AbstractIntegrationTest starts Postgres and Redis Testcontainers with @DynamicPropertySource and lets Flyway migrate the schema

CreateShortUrlIT asserts 201 + short_url shape + persisted row (created_by null, code_source set), 400 problem+json with no row persisted, 409 on taken alias with the existing mapping unchanged, and distinct codes for a repeated long_url
RedirectIT asserts 302 + Location + Cache-Control: private, 404 for unknown code, 410 for expired code, all errors application/problem+json

CacheAndFallbackIT proves a cache hit serves the redirect, TTL <= remaining expiry, and that a stopped/unreachable Redis still yields 201 with code_source db_sequence on write and a 302 served from Postgres on read
ProfileSeparationIT boots with spring.profiles.active=read (POST -> 404) and =write (GET -> 404) and verifies the default profile serves both

OpenApiContractIT compares the springdoc-generated document from the running context against the committed src/main/resources/openapi.yaml operation-by-operation and status-code-by-status-code and fails on drift
All IT classes are named *IT so they only run under `./mvnw -q -Pit verify`; `./mvnw -q test` stays container-free and `./mvnw -q -Pit verify` passes
tasks.risk_notes: Highest-effort task: Testcontainers availability, Redis-outage simulation and springdoc/committed-document parity are the main failure modes. If the generated document differs from the handwritten one, the contract gate fails - align the handwritten file with the springdoc dump produced by the it profile.
tasks.rollback_note: Delete src/main/resources/openapi.yaml and the it test package; unit gates still pass but the contract and integration gates will fail until re-done.

tasks.title: Release artifacts: Dockerfile, CI workflow and README
definition_of_done: Dockerfile is a multi-stage build (Maven/JDK 25 build stage using ./mvnw -DskipTests package, slim JRE runtime stage) running the fat jar as a non-root user, exposing 8080, parameterising SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE and containing no secrets or hard-coded credentials

.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on push/pull_request and executes ./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile, ./mvnw -q spotless:check (advisory), ./mvnw -q -Dtest=ArchitectureTest test, ./mvnw -q test and ./mvnw -q -Pit verify, with no secrets inlined

README.md documents the service, endpoints (POST /api/v1/urls, GET /{short_code}), the read/write/default Spring profile deployment model, configuration properties (base URL, counter batch size, cache TTL), code_source semantics, how to run locally and with Docker, and points at src/main/resources/openapi.yaml
docs/operations.md records the Redis-outage degradation behaviour and the accepted counter gaps (AMB-10)
Release gate satisfied: Dockerfile, a .github/workflows workflow, README.md and the committed OpenAPI document all exist; all required gates pass on the whole repository
tasks.risk_notes: Touches protected paths (Dockerfile, .github/workflows/**). CI must not invoke commands the sandbox cannot run and must never reference forbidden files (.env, keys, secrets/**).
tasks.rollback_note: Delete Dockerfile, .github/workflows/ci.yml, README.md and docs/operations.md; application code and tests remain intact, only the release gate regresses.

rationale: Greenfield Java build sequenced so every required gate has an owner and no task is blocked on unfinished contracts. T1 front-loads all protected build/config surface (pom dependencies, the `it` profile with failsafe + springdoc dump, application*.yml profiles) because compile/unit/integration/contract gates all depend on it; getting it wrong later would invalidate everything downstream, hence HIGH. T2 (protected Flyway migration, entity, repository) and T3 (DTO validation rules + problem+json advice) are independent of each other and run in parallel as the data and error contracts. T4 isolates the trickiest algorithmic piece - the batched Redis INCRBY allocator with Postgres-sequence fallback and code_source - so its concurrency and failure-mode tests stand alone. T5 and T6 then implement the two independently deployable HTTP surfaces in parallel, each profile-gated (@Profile("!read") / @Profile("!write")) in separate packages so their allowed_files never overlap. T7 consolidates the contract gate: the committed src/main/resources/openapi.yaml plus Testcontainers ITs (Postgres + Redis) that cover every acceptance criterion end-to-end, including cache hits, Redis-outage degradation on both paths, profile separation, and springdoc-vs-committed-document parity. T8 finishes the release checklist (Dockerfile, CI workflow, README, ops doc) last, when the commands it wires into CI are known-good; it touches protected infra paths so it is HIGH. Every task that changes src/** ships its tests in the same task, each stays well under 15 files, and only allowed/protected paths are touched - the orchestrator-provisioned mvnw and sdlc/ArchitectureTest.java are never listed.  Note: the spec's open ambiguities AMB-9/10/11 are implemented at their documented defaults (24h default cache TTL, gaps allowed on restart, counter seeded so generated codes are >= 3 chars) and are flagged for confirmation rather than silently re-decided.
